name: Whalebone Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA's own site page (exploreparks/site/whalebone-beach) names it as a scenic beach between rocky headlands, for fishing and walking; a second-tier beach a real source names keeps.
objection: Remote: reached only by 4WD when the track is open, otherwise on foot via the Hakea Trail; both counted sources are DBCA (not independent), and few visitors get there.

name: West Mount Barren
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage's Fitzgerald River NP page; a summit/ridgeline walk (about 2 h return) with sweeping park and coast views.
objection: None strong; overlaps the Barren Range entry, which should not also be kept.

name: Barren Range
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of West Mount Barren (and East Mount Barren): the range is a landscape seen along the park, and its visitable points are the individual peaks, kept separately.
objection: Wikivoyage lists the Barren Range as a See item in its own right; if neither Mount Barren were kept, the range would be the spot.

name: Quoin Head
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page calls it one of the park's most spectacular headlands, popular with photographers, with a bay, beach and campground; Wikivoyage lists its campsite.
objection: Remote, 4WD access; both counted sources are DBCA.

name: St Mary Inlet
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page names it (scenic inlet behind the dunes near Point Ann, birdwatching, shore walk at low water, campground). Case for: a named visitor site with a campground listed by Wikivoyage. Case against: rule 3, it sits beside Point Ann (the park's whale-watching point) and may be part of that visit rather than a distinct draw.
objection: No formal paths; the visit is mainly camping or a look on the way to Point Ann.

name: Hamersley Inlet
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (deep inlet in a winding valley, birdlife, beach, picnic and camping) and Wikivoyage lists its campsite; a second-tier inlet stop at the end of Hamersley Drive.
objection: One agency page plus a Wikivoyage camping line; a quiet place mostly for campers.

name: Hellfire Bay
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback. The DBCA page places Hellfire Bay in Cape Le Grand National Park (Esperance), not Fitzgerald River NP as the candidate note says.
objection: It is a strong draw in its own region; the golden-outback pass must cover it.

name: Hakea Trail
reason: Rule 1: named only as a DBCA gallery caption and as the foot route to Whalebone Beach; DBCA has no trail page for it (exploreparks /trail/hakea-trail 404). Case for: a coastal walk through the park's plant diversity linking Quoin Head and Whalebone Beach. Case against: one weak mention, and rule 3, it may be best folded into Whalebone Beach/Quoin Head.
objection: No length, trailhead or trail page found; a gallery caption is a thin source.

name: Hamersley Drive
reason: Rule 3 / 'a spot is a place': a road through the park named only in a DBCA gallery caption; its stops (Hamersley Inlet, East Mount Barren) are the places and are judged on their own.
objection: It is the park's main sealed scenic route and could carry a drive spot if the owner allows drives.

name: Mount Hassell
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page for a Stirling Range summit walk (moderately difficult, wildflowers, views to Toolbrunup); a real 2-3 h climb in the park. Location confirmed in Stirling Range NP (Great Southern).
objection: One counted source, and a lesser peak beside Toolbrunup; an owner could treat it as marginal.

name: Dillon Bay
reason: Re-looked: no counted source found (only ExplorOz, BeachSafe and campsite directories, plus Wikipedia's Bremer Bay page). Case for: a sheltered bay south of Bremer Bay with Blossoms Beach (4WD beach driving), camping and fishing, partly in Fitzgerald River NP. Case against: rule 1 fails without a visitor-oriented source; it reads as a locals' fishing spot.
objection: No tourism board, DBCA or guidebook names it; ExplorOz and BeachSafe are not counted sources.

name: Denmark Historical Museum
reason: Rule 1: one counted source, a Wikivoyage See listing (16 Mitchell St, local history of Denmark's timber and industrial times). Case for: open to the public, a half-hour indoor visit. Case against: a small volunteer local-history museum with limited hours; the friend test says only if nearby, and it needs a second source.
objection: Single source, short visit, local interest only.

name: Ocean Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found a counted source, Tourism WA's attraction page (westernaustralia.com/au/attraction/ocean-beach), plus Wikivoyage Denmark naming it as within cycling reach; Denmark's patrolled surf beach at the mouth of Wilson Inlet with a lookout, surf club and walks.
objection: Strong rips near the inlet; a beach mainly for surfers in cool water.

name: Denmark Wineries
reason: Not a place: a grouping of many cellar doors around Denmark; the winery rule keeps only an estate a visitor source singles out as a destination, and none is named here.
objection: Wine is a major reason people visit Denmark; that belongs in the destination description, not a spot.

name: Mount Frankland National Park
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. Wikipedia places the park in the South West region, and the neighbouring localities (North Walpole, Broke) are in the Shire of Manjimup.
objection: DBCA files it under Walpole and the boundary runs close; if the owner puts the line at Walpole's catchment, it is a clear keep (DBCA park page, summit trail and wilderness lookout, Walpole Visitor Centre names it). The south-west pass must cover it.

name: Walpole-Nornalup National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA park page (tingle and karri forest, inlets, Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk, Hilltop, Bibbulmun Track) and the Walpole Visitor Centre's explore page; a flagship forest park.
objection: Most of its draws are separate candidates (Valley of the Giants, Giant Tingle Tree, Circular Pool, Coalmine Beach); the park as a spot must take its own visitor point, not one of theirs.

name: Giant Tingle Tree
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre (largest-girthed living eucalypt, an 800 m circular walk from the Hilltop Road car park); a distinct forest giant.
objection: Shares Hilltop Road with Hilltop Lookout; may be seen as part of one Hilltop drive.

name: Hilltop Lookout
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre name it (forest-clearing view over the Frankland River, Nornalup Inlet and the Southern Ocean). Case for: two sources and a real view. Case against: rule 3, a short stop on the same one-way Hilltop Road as the Giant Tingle Tree, about 1 km apart; could be folded into that spot.
objection: A ten-minute look on the way to the Giant Tingle Tree.

name: Circular Pool
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (Frankland River pool and rapids, two viewing platforms, boardwalk, picnic area) and the Walpole Visitor Centre names it; a popular picnic and walking stop.
objection: Short visit, mainly a picnic spot.

name: Coalmine Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (family swimming and paddling beach on Nornalup Inlet, picnic area, boat and kayak launch) and the Walpole Visitor Centre names it.
objection: An inlet beach mainly used by those staying at the adjacent holiday park.

name: Irwin Inlet
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page only (picnic, boating and fishing; sand spit reached by 4WD from Peaceful Bay). Case for: a named DBCA visitor site. Case against: one source, and visitors mostly reach it from Peaceful Bay, which is kept; a quiet fishing spot rather than a draw.
objection: Locals' fishing spot; overlaps Peaceful Bay.

name: Mount Clare
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (summit trail through tingle and karri to Southern Ocean views, picnic area, Deep River loop) and the Walpole Visitor Centre lists it among half-day walks.
objection: Candidate flagged as a disambiguation: confirm it is the Walpole Wilderness Mount Clare (not Albany's Mount Clarence) before pinning.

name: Conspicuous Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page 'Conspicuous Cliff' (limestone cliffs, surf beach, lookouts, whale watching, Bibbulmun day walk to Rame Head) and the Walpole Visitor Centre; 13 km east of Walpole. Keep as one spot under DBCA's name, Conspicuous Cliff.
objection: None strong; name choice (Cliff vs Beach) to settle with the proposer.

name: Granite Skywalk
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Porongurup park page; a suspended walkway on Castle Rock with lookouts to Albany and the Stirling Range, a 4.4 km return walk. Keep as one with Castle Rock (the board lists 'Castle Rock'): duplicate of Castle Rock if that is kept, the skywalk is the named attraction.
objection: Two names for one walk and rock; must not ship as two spots.

name: Devils Slide
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA's Porongurup page lists the Devils Slide walk (5 km, 2 h, highest Porongurup peak, views north and south) and Mountain Country Tourism (Mount Barker's visitor centre) has a trail page; a distinct summit walk.
objection: Shares a trailhead area with the Tree in the Rock circuit; secondary to the Granite Skywalk.

name: Gibraltar Rock
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found no counted source; only climbing guides (UKClimbing) describe it, reached by an unmarked 4WD track and taped path, and DBCA lists no visitor site or trail for it.
objection: A prominent Porongurup monolith with a Wikipedia article; a climbers' crag could be a draw for a niche.

name: Castle Rock Estate
reason: Winery rule: a cellar door named once in a board itinerary PDF, not singled out as a destination in its own right; one of many Great Southern cellar doors.
objection: The board's highlights itinerary does name it, and it has views of the Stirling Range.

name: Mount Trio
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Stirling Range park page; a steep summit walk to three summits linked by a plateau with a picnic area at the trailhead.
objection: Lesser-known than Bluff Knoll and Toolbrunup; both sources are DBCA.

name: Toolbrunup Peak
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and park page; the Stirling Range's second-highest peak, a hard scramble with 360-degree views.
objection: Both sources are DBCA; a fit-walkers' summit.

name: Stirling Range Scenic Drive
reason: Rule 1: DBCA's Stirling Range park page names the 42 km mostly unsealed scenic drive through the heart of the park with stops. Case for: the main non-hiking way to see the range, a real half-day outing. Case against: 'a spot is a place': a road, whose stops (peaks, lookouts, picnic areas) are the places; it overlaps the park itself.
objection: Drives are routes, not places; it duplicates the park.

name: Cape Riche
reason: Re-looked: one counted source, Visit Albany's (amazingalbany.com.au) nature-based camping page, which names Cape Riche as a caretaker-run campground; the City of Albany camping page agrees. Case for: a remote cape for fishing, swimming, snorkelling, headland rock walks and Mount Melville. Case against: named only as a campground, no source describes a sight; one source.
objection: A campground listing is not a visitor 'See' entry; mostly anglers and campers.

name: Puntapin Rock
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (4 km south-east of Wagin in the Wheatbelt, per Wikipedia).
objection: Wikipedia cites a Golden Outback holiday planner, so the golden-outback pass may find a counted source.

name: Oyster Harbour
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (swimming beaches, picnic areas, fishing, boat cruises up the Kalgan River). Case for: a counted source naming it as a family outing. Case against: rule 3, the harbour is a water body visited from Emu Point on its southern shore (kept); as a spot it is a near-duplicate of Emu Point.
objection: Its visitor point is Emu Point.

name: King George Sound
reason: Rule 3: a body of water, seen from the places on its shore (Middleton Beach, Emu Point, Torndirrup lookouts, Princess Royal Fortress); no counted source names it as a place to go, and whale-watching tours on it are operators.
objection: A highly viewed article and the setting of Albany's whale watching; its visitor experience is captured by the shore spots.

name: Valley of the Giants
reason: Rule 1+2: Australia's South West board listing and DBCA's Walpole-Nornalup page (Tree Top Walk 40 m up in the tingle canopy, Ancient Empire). Keep as one with 'Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk' (also a board listing): duplicate of that entry, one spot.
objection: Two board listings for the same site; must not ship twice.

name: The Kodja Place
reason: Rule 1+2: Australia's South West board listing and its own site: Kojonup's cultural centre with the Kodj Gallery, Storyplace, Australian Rose Maze and Noongar stories; a real indoor visit. Note: it is in Kojonup, not Albany as the candidate note says (still Great Southern).
objection: One counted source; a small-town centre visitors mostly reach passing through on the Albany Highway.

name: Museum of the Great Southern
reason: Rule 1+2: Australia's South West board listing and the WA Museum's own page: Albany's branch of the state museum on Residency Road, open daily 10-4, free, with the Brig Amity replica and natural and social history galleries. Keep as one with any 'Residency Museum' or 'Brig Amity' candidate.
objection: Candidate coordinates are the WA Museum in Perth (redirect); the pin must be resolved at Residency Road, Albany. Wikivoyage lists the Residency Museum and the Brig Amity separately, a duplication risk.

name: Honeymoon Pool
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west (Honeymoon Pool is in Wellington National Park near Collie, Worsley 6225, per OpenStreetMap).
objection: A popular swimming hole; the south-west pass must cover it.

name: Denmark Animal Farm and Pentland Alpaca Stud
reason: Rule 1: Australia's South West board listing and its own site (animal park, open every day 10-4, WA's first alpaca farm, about 50 alpacas). Case for: a permanent, open, family visitor farm. Case against: rule 2/business: largely a gift shop and petting farm, and the friend test says only if nearby; one source.
objection: A small commercial farm attraction with a shop.

name: Denmark Chocolate Company
reason: Business rule: a chocolate maker and shop, not a place to see.
objection: The board lists it; tastings draw some visitors.

name: Albany Tours
reason: Operator: a tour company, not a place; the places it visits are the spots.
objection: None.

name: Kaarl Wirn Cultural Tours Albany
reason: Operator: an Aboriginal cultural tour operator, not a place; the places it visits are the spots.
objection: Cultural tours are a strong reason to visit; mention them in the destination's text.

name: WOW Wilderness EcoCruise
reason: Operator: a cruise on the Walpole and Nornalup inlets; the place is the inlets (Coalmine Beach and the park are kept).
objection: A well-known Walpole experience; mention it in the place's bio.

name: Whale Watch Western Australia
reason: Operator: a whale-watching company, not a place.
objection: None.

name: The Lake House Denmark
reason: Business rule: accommodation, restaurant and cellar door, not a landmark estate a guide singles out.
objection: The board lists it.

name: Fernhook Falls
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. OpenStreetMap places it in North Walpole, a locality of the Shire of Manjimup, in Mount Frankland South NP.
objection: A clear keep on the merits (DBCA site page and Walpole Visitor Centre); the south-west pass must cover it.

name: East Mount Barren
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page: a 450 m quartzite peak on the Southern Ocean with a summit walk from the western car park and views over the park; a distinct draw near Hopetoun but inside Fitzgerald River NP (Great Southern per the brief).
objection: One counted source; a hard short climb.

name: Lights Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (beach on the Bibbulmun Track just east of William Bay NP for surfing, fishing, walking and sightseeing); a second-tier Denmark beach a real source names.
objection: Rule 3 risk: close to Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks; the DBCA page sits under Greens Pool.

name: Mandalay Beach
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. DBCA places it in D'Entrecasteaux NP, and OpenStreetMap places it in Broke, a locality of the Shire of Manjimup.
objection: A clear keep on the merits (DBCA, Walpole Visitor Centre, the 1911 wreck); the south-west pass must cover it.

name: Emu Point
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (calm, shallow swimming beach, picnic lawns, fishing, boating, windsurfing) on Oyster Harbour; Wikivoyage Albany names the Middleton Beach-Emu Point path.
objection: Partly a suburb and holiday-park area; it is the visitor point of Oyster Harbour, so the two must not both ship.

name: Peaceful Bay
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found the Walpole Visitor Centre explore page: a coastal village 33 km east of Walpole with turquoise water for swimming, snorkelling and fishing; a second-tier beach village.
objection: One counted source; a holiday-shack village.

name: Mount Romance Sandalwood Factory
reason: Business rule: a sandalwood factory and shop with product tours, named only in an accommodation directory (WA Holiday Guide), not a counted visitor source.
objection: It offers daily information tours, which some visitors take.

name: Plantagenet Wines
reason: Winery rule: a business-directory listing (Mountain Country Tourism) of a cellar door; the region's first winery (1975) but not singled out by a visitor source as a destination in its own right.
objection: Historic as the Great Southern's first winery.

name: Mount Barker Wineries
reason: Not a place: a grouping of the sub-region's wineries (Mount Barker Wine Producers' list); the winery rule keeps only a singled-out estate.
objection: Wine touring is a reason to visit; belongs in destination text.

name: Bornholm
reason: Rule 1/3: a rural locality with no visitor source and nothing named to see; its coast is West Cape Howe NP, judged separately. (Candidate coordinates and views belong to the Danish island.)
objection: None.

name: Wilson Inlet
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (paddling, kayak and canoe hire, fishing, the 12 km Wilson Inlet Heritage Trail to Crusoe Beach, inlet cruises). Case for: a counted source and a range of things to do. Case against: rule 3, a water body whose visitor points are Ocean Beach (kept) and Denmark's riverfront; the Heritage Trail might be the better spot.
objection: A 20 km water body has no single visitor point; overlaps Ocean Beach.
